items.title: Commencement
notes:
A meeting of City Council was held at 5:02 p.m. this date, chaired by Mayor B. Vrbanovic. Notice of this meeting had been previously given to all members of Council by the City Clerk pursuant to Chapter 25 (Council Procedure) of the Municipal Code.

The meeting began with a Land Acknowledgement given by the Mayor.

items.title: Disclosure of Pecuniary Interest and the General Nature Thereof
Federation of Canadian Municipalities (FCM) Delegate Presentation – PMI WILL Service Initiative Update
notes:
Mayor B. Vrbanovic welcomed colleagues from Sri Lanka, along with our partners from the Federation of Canadian Municipalities (FCM), to this Special Council meeting as part of the Partnerships for Municipal Innovation – Women in Local Leadership initiative. Mayor B. Vrbanovic advised that the City of Kitchener is proud to partner with the Town of Cobourg and Sri Lankan local governments through FCM, with funding from Global Affairs Canada, on this important six-year program that strengthens women’s leadership and supports inclusive, gender responsive municipal services. Mayor Vrbanovic welcomed Christine Eloy, Operations Manager at the Federation of Canadian Municipalities to provide an overview of the program and its impacts.

Sue Weare, Community Engagement Consultant, Chadini Ramanayake, National Project Coordinator, Sivaram Rajaweeran, Secretary of Council, Iruka Weerarathne, Chairman/Mayor of the Council, Thirunavukkarasu Arulchelvan, Technical Officer of the Council, Sagara Kumara, Chairman/Mayor of the Council all program participants, shared their experiences in the program, as well as how this program has impacted their communities. C. Ramanayake then responded to questions from Council.

Councillor S. Davey left and re-entered the meeting at this time.

Mayor B. Vrbanovic and members of Council then presented them with a token of appreciation our colleagues from Sri Lanka a gift as a token of appreciation, friendship and partnership.

items.title: Recess and Reconvene
notes: The Special Council then recessed at 6:28 p.m. and reconvened at 10:18 p.m. chaired by Mayor B. Vrbanovic, with all members present. Councillor A. Owodunni was participating electronically.

items.title: Finance and Corporate Services Committee Report - April 20, 2026
Council Compensation Review Findings, CAO-2026-172
notes:
Council considered the following item, Council Compensation Review Findings, CAO-2026-172, which was considered at the Finance and Corporate Services Committee meeting earlier this date.

Councillor S. Davey brought forward the recommendation, which was seconded by Councillor B. Ioannidis.

Councillor C. Michaud brought forward an amendment, which was seconded by Councillor S. Davey to approve compensation for the Mayor, as outlined in Report CAO-2026-172, rather than an increase of 10.3%.

Councillor A. Owodunni entered the meeting at this time.

Councillor C. Michaud's amendment was then voted on and was Carried.

The following motion was then voted on.

motions.text: "That the council compensation recommendations prepared by Marianne Love Consulting Services Ltd., as appended to Corporate Services Department report CAO-2026-172, be approved effective for the 2026-2030 term of council; and, That staff be directed to amend GOV-COU-020 (Council Compensation) in accordance with report CAO-2026-172; and, That the differential between the 50th and 60th percentile identified in Report CAO‑2026‑172 be funded through Kitchener Utilities - in recognition of Council’s unique governing responsibility for the municipally owned gas utility; and further, That staff be directed to undertake a Council compensation review in advance of the 2030 election cycle and should include all considerations raised through the compensation report raised by Marianne Love Consulting Services Ltd."
motions.text_html:
"That the council compensation recommendations prepared by Marianne Love Consulting Services Ltd., as appended to Corporate Services Department report CAO-2026-172, be approved effective for the 2026-2030 term of council; and,

That staff be directed to amend GOV-COU-020 (Council Compensation) in accordance with report CAO-2026-172; and,

That the differential between the 50th and 60th percentile identified in Report CAO‑2026‑172 be funded through Kitchener Utilities - in recognition of Council’s unique governing responsibility for the municipally owned gas utility; and further,

motions.item_title: Notice of Motion - S. Stretch - Localized Traffic Impacts at Victoria St N and Ahrens St W
motions.text: "WHEREAS localized traffic impacts are being experienced along Victoria Street North at Ahrens Street West during train arrival and departure times at the existing Kitchener Go/VIA station; WHEREAS Region of Waterloo staff have acknowledged that the Region is responsible for sidewalk snow clearing along the Regional and Metrolinx properties on Victoria Street; THEREFORE BE IT RESOLVED that staff be directed work with Regional Staff to review temporary and permanent modifications to the signalized intersection at Victoria Street North and Ahrens Street West, including but not limited to potential left turn restrictions and stop bar placement to improve traffic flow and intersection operations; and, THEREFORE BE IT FINALLY RESOLVED that staff be directed to work with Regional Staff to improve winter maintenance along the Regional and Metrolinx properties prior to Winter 2026."
motions.text_html:
"WHEREAS localized traffic impacts are being experienced along Victoria Street North at Ahrens Street West during train arrival and departure times at the existing Kitchener Go/VIA station;

WHEREAS Region of Waterloo staff have acknowledged that the Region is responsible for sidewalk snow clearing along the Regional and Metrolinx properties on Victoria Street; 

THEREFORE BE IT RESOLVED that staff be directed work with Regional Staff to review temporary and permanent modifications to the signalized intersection at Victoria Street North and Ahrens Street West, including but not limited to potential left turn restrictions and stop bar placement to improve traffic flow and intersection operations; and,

THEREFORE BE IT FINALLY RESOLVED that staff be directed to work with Regional Staff to improve winter maintenance along the Regional and Metrolinx properties prior to Winter 2026."

motions.item_title: Notice of Motion - S. Stretch - Community Communications Plan around Transit Hub and GO Expansion
motions.text: "WHEREAS improved local and inter-regional transit provides an overall net benefit for Kitchener residents; WHEREAS Progress toward dedicated GO rail service on the Kitchener Line is underway following a 2025 agreement in principle with CN, alongside recent service enhancements, including 18 new weekend trips and the first ever weekend service to Kitchener; WHEREAS construction of the Kitchener Central Transit Hub (KCTH) and GO Expansion will be a multi-year project and will have multi-year localized community impacts during construction including, but not limited to noise, active transportation and traffic disruption and detours; WHEREAS The impact to the community immediately surrounding the build site and impacted by this construction should receive honest and direct communication; WHEREAS proactive project updates and communication are important factors in ensuring residents, businesses, neighbourhood associations and elected officials are informed during significant capital construction projects; THEREFORE BE IT RESOLVED that staff be directed to coordinate with the Region of Waterloo and Metrolinx on a communications plan and to set community meetings before 2027 and ongoing to inform and connect with residents, businesses, neighbourhood associations and elected officials throughout the multi-year construction process."
motions.text_html:
"WHEREAS improved local and inter-regional transit provides an overall net benefit for Kitchener residents;

WHEREAS Progress toward dedicated GO rail service on the Kitchener Line is underway following a 2025 agreement in principle with CN, alongside recent service enhancements, including 18 new weekend trips and the first ever weekend service to Kitchener; 

WHEREAS construction of the Kitchener Central Transit Hub (KCTH) and GO Expansion will be a multi-year project and will have multi-year localized community impacts during construction including, but not limited to noise, active transportation and traffic disruption and detours;

WHEREAS The impact to the community immediately surrounding the build site and impacted by this construction should receive honest and direct communication;

WHEREAS proactive project updates and communication are important factors in ensuring residents, businesses, neighbourhood associations and elected officials are informed during significant capital construction projects;

THEREFORE BE IT RESOLVED that staff be directed to coordinate with the Region of Waterloo and Metrolinx on a communications plan and to set community meetings before 2027 and ongoing to inform and connect with residents, businesses, neighbourhood associations and elected officials throughout the multi-year construction process."
